review_conclusions: registeredAt is used only by registration creation, strict schema validation, serialization and the new cleanup; matching, amount, expiry and recovery consumers do not read it.

A v1 registration still requires a positive numeric save time. A v2 registration requires exactly registeredAt:null and is accepted inside document v4 only. Legacy v1-v3 documents remain readable; ordinary legacy writes remain v3.
Preview contains only a frozen category/count. Its identity is held in a per-handle WeakMap with encrypted snapshot text and session revision; no plaintext invoice or timestamp snapshot is retained.
Confirmation consumes the preview before awaiting work, rechecks exact ciphertext and authority, and makes a single guarded CAS attempt without optimistic retry. Zero eligible records cause no write.
Session replacement, same-key unlock, lock, different handle, cancellation, caller consent revocation, intervening writes, unknown formats and saturated safety state do not authorize cleanup.

Transformation changes only document version and v1 registration version/registeredAt. Matching times, net amounts, identities, complete observations, receipts, reorg cutoff/tombstones and unrelated stores remain intact.

Existing local redaction survives duplicate registration and older-backup import; new imported rows retain their metadata until a fresh approval. The documented later deletion of an entire registration is a separate operation and creates no new deletion-history store.
The actual ledger wires separate default-off consent to the current unlocked vault. Cancel, quick-hide, scope/session changes and pending-action guards revoke the preview or write authority.

All ten new UI messages are classified as security-sensitive. All existing entries in each of the four catalogs remain unchanged; source-English fallback remains subject to the existing translation-review policy.

The two native browser cases use real static UI, actual encrypted backup inspection, external-request blocking and native storage. They cover ordinary cleanup/import/reload and concurrent registration from another tab; collection succeeded but execution did not occur in this review.
